title: createStore: Fine-Grained Deep Proxy Path Mutation Tracking

progressiveExplaining.eli5: If you have a giant notebook with 1,000 pages of data and change a single word on page 500, a regular signal forces you to photocopy all 1,000 pages. Solid's `createStore` places tiny individual sensor wires on every single line of every single page: changing word #3 on page 500 triggers only the person reading that exact line, without touching the rest of the book.
progressiveExplaining.junior: `createStore` creates deeply reactive tree structures (objects and arrays). `const [state, setState] = createStore({ user: { profile: { name: 'Ada' } }, todos: [] });`. Unlike `createSignal` (where updating a nested field requires cloning the entire parent object), `createStore` uses path-based setters: `setState('user', 'profile', 'name', 'Grace')`. Only components reading that exact nested property update.
progressiveExplaining.senior: Architecturally, `createStore` uses shallow, lazy JavaScript Proxies generated on demand during property traversal. It implements fine-grained nested reactivity: accessing `state.user.profile.name` subscribes only to the leaf `name` signal node. When updating via path selectors or utilities like `produce()` (Immer-like mutation syntax) or `reconcile()` (diffing incoming API arrays by ID), Solid mutates data in place and triggers only the affected leaf subscribers, completely bypassing parent object invalidation.
progressiveExplaining.underTheHood: Under the hood, `createStore` wraps objects in a recursive `Proxy` using `get` traps. Each property lookup checks an internal `WeakMap` for a property-specific signal. When `setState('todos', 2, 'done', true)` runs, Solid traverses the internal target tree, modifies the property in place, and calls `write()` on only the target property's signal. `reconcile(newArray)` performs a key-based diff against existing proxy objects, reusing existing proxy instances and updating only changed properties.

rosettaStone.react: Immer `produce` or Zustand creating immutable object clones on every mutation.

codeComparison.title: Signal Object Cloning vs Solid Store Surgical Path Update
codeComparison.summary: Updating nested objects in signals requires immutable cloning of all parent levels; `createStore` modifies leaf properties directly.

legacyOrBad.label: createSignal Object Cloning
legacyOrBad.snippet: setUser(u => ({ ...u, profile: { ...u.profile, name: 'Grace' } })); // ❌ Full tree cloning

modernOrGood.label: createStore Path Mutation
modernOrGood.snippet: setState('profile', 'name', 'Grace'); // ✅ NEW: Zero cloning, updates only 'name' subscribers

interviewGotchas.question: What does the `reconcile()` store utility do when handling new data from an API response?
interviewGotchas.contextIntro: Interviewers test your knowledge of backend API integration with fine-grained stores.
interviewGotchas.detailedAnswer: When replacing a store array or object with a fresh API response (`setUser(reconcile(freshData))`), `reconcile()` diffs the new data against the existing store objects by key/ID. It applies updates only to fields that changed, preserves unchanged object references, and avoids triggering unneeded subscriber notifications, preventing UI flicker.
interviewGotchas.trapWarning: Using `setState(freshData)` directly without `reconcile()` replaces all object references, forcing all components reading any property of the store to re-evaluate.

interviewGotchas.question: Why does wrapping store state in `unwrap(store)` exist, and when should you use it?
interviewGotchas.contextIntro: Checks understanding of proxy unwrapping for external library interop.
interviewGotchas.detailedAnswer: `unwrap(state)` strips the reactive Proxy wrappers and returns the underlying raw JavaScript object tree. This is necessary when passing data to third-party non-reactive libraries (like charting libraries, Web Workers via `postMessage`, or `structuredClone`), which can fail or degrade in performance if given Proxy instances.
interviewGotchas.trapWarning: Do not mutate the object returned by `unwrap()`; raw mutations bypass the reactivity graph and will not notify UI subscribers.
